item.title: 🗓 On August 31 – September 1, 2026, President of Russia Vladimir Putin visited Bishkek
item.description: 🗓 On August 31 – September 1, 2026, President of Russia Vladimir Putin visited Bishkek , where he took part in the events of the anniversary Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation ( #SCO ), marking the Organisation’s 25th anniversary. Key events of the anniversary Summit: 👏 Opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games 🎙 Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State 🎙 SCO Plus meeting 💬 From Vladimir Putin’s remarks at the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State: Over the past 25 years, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has come a long way, becoming one of the independent and influential centres of the emerging #MultipolarWorld . Today, the SCO is effectively the largest regional association not only on our common Eurasian continent, but in the world as a whole. Its member states account for almost half of the world’s population and more than one-third of global GDP. ✍️ Following the meeting, a package of 28 documents was adopted, including the Bishkek Declaration on the 25th Anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation . *** 🤝 On the sidelines of the Summit, Vladimir Putin held bilateral meetings with: 🇨🇳 President of China Xi Jinping 🇮🇳 Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi 🇺🇿 President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev 🇰🇿 President of Kazakhstan Kassym-Jomart Tokayev 🇮🇷 President of Iran Masoud Pezeshkian 🇹🇯 President of Tajikistan Emomali Rahmon 🇹🇷 President of Turkiye Recep Tayyip Erdogan 🇲🇳 President of Mongolia Ukhnaagiin Khurelsukh 🇦🇲 Prime Mini

🗓
On August 31 – September 1, 2026,
President of Russia Vladimir Putin
visited Bishkek
, where he took part in the events of the
anniversary Summit of
the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
(
#SCO
), marking the Organisation’s 25th anniversary.
Key events of the anniversary Summit:
👏
Opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games
🎙
Meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State
🎙
SCO Plus meeting
💬
From
Vladimir Putin’s remarks
at the meeting of the SCO Council of Heads of State:
Over the past 25 years, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has come a long way, becoming one of the independent and influential centres of the emerging
#MultipolarWorld
.
Today, the SCO is effectively the largest regional association not only on our common Eurasian continent, but in the world as a whole.
Its member states account for almost half of the world’s population and more than one-third of global GDP.
✍️
Following the meeting,
a package of 28 documents
was adopted, including
the Bishkek Declaration on the 25th Anniversary of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation
.
***
🤝
On the sidelines of the Summit,
Vladimir Putin held bilateral meetings
with:
🇨🇳
President of China Xi Jinping
🇮🇳
Prime Minister of India Narendra Modi
🇺🇿
President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev
🇰🇿

🇮🇷

🇹🇯

🇹🇷

🇰🇬
President of Kyrgyzstan Sadyr Japarov

🎙
Concluding his working visit to Kyrgyzstan,
Vladimir Putin answered questions from Russian journalists
, addressing key issues on the international agenda.

🗓️
On 1 September 2026, on the margins of
the 67th session of the Working Group B of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission
, an event was held with the support of the Permanent Mission of the Russian Federation, focusing on
the potential application of national artificial intelligence (AI) technologies
in support of the Organization’s activities
The event brought together
more than 120 participants
, including representatives of CTBTO Preparatory Commission Member States - diplomats and national experts - as well as officials of the Organization’s Provisional Technical Secretariat
🇷🇺
In his opening remarks, Deputy Permanent Representative
Roman Ustinov
emphasized that any potential introduction of AI into the work of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission should be approached with particular caution, taking into account, inter alia, the need to protect sensitive information; preserve human responsibility and the decisive role of human judgement in the use of AI; ensure transparency of the models employed; conduct a prior assessment of associated risks; and maintain accountability to the Organization’s policymaking organs
A central element of the event was a presentation by Professor
Evgeny Burnaev
, Vice President for AI Development and Director of the Skoltech AI Center, who outlined potential pilot projects demonstrating the capabilities of
Russian AI technologies
for possible use in support of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission
The solutions presented by Professor Burnaev are intended
to complement the Organization’s existing working mechanisms with tools
for intelligent data analysis and forecasting
The event generated
considerable professional interest among the diplomatic and expert communities
. In view of the importance and complexity of substantive discussions on this topic, consideration has been initiated regarding the possible establishment of
a dedicated expert group on the application of AI
in the activities of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission

🎙
Answers
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin to media questions following his working visit to Kyrgyzstan
(Bishkek, September 1, 2026)
Key points
:
#RussiaUS
•
Contacts between Russia and the US have always existed
, even during the most difficult periods of the Cold War,
and they continue today
.
• Direct contacts are maintained between the Heads of the intelligence services. Quite recently,
we returned a US citizen to the American Side
who had been serving a prison sentence in Russia.
• We are absolutely comfortable working with people we know well and generally trust. They are close to President Trump, sincere people who are trying to give our work concrete substance. And President Trump trusts them, which is very important.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are therefore
always welcome guests in Russia
, and we are pleased to work with them.
#UkrainianCrisis
#NATO
•
We believe that negotiations
– any negotiations –
should above all have concrete substance
. If someone is capable of making a positive contribution to a negotiating process that is currently, to a certain extent,
frozen
, we have no objection
.
What is needed here are specialists, military experts and diplomats.
• The collective West was given a very apt description back in Soviet times –
the sharks of imperialism.
If anyone tries to drag us down the food chain and devour us,
they may well get their teeth knocked out.
Russia is ready to do that, despite the rapidly growing appetites – and teeth – of these sharks.
• Despite everything,
Russian forces
continue to increase the pace of their advance
in
the special military operation
zone.
• Strikes continue against Ukrainian military facilities, industrial enterprises, ports and logistics infrastructure used in the interests of the Ukrainian armed forces –
in response
, as is well known,
to the Kiev regime’s continuing attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure, fuel and energy facilities and oil refineries.
❗️
Any military facilities in Ukraine are legitimate targets for us
– British or otherwise.
•
The Russian Armed Forces
have been instructed to prepare and carry out
large-scale strikes against Ukraine’s energy facilities. They strike ours – they will get a response.
#Germany
#Leipzig
•
As for the actions of the German authorities
,
they are primarily driven by Germany’s domestic political situation.
• Chancellor Merz is in a difficult domestic political position and does not enjoy the confidence of his citizens. It is clear why:
he is not defending Germany’s national interests, but trading them away.
There are obvious economic failures – businesses are closing, people are losing their jobs and living standards are falling.
• [
Germany's recent move
]
is yet another mistake –
a serious one
–
and, in my view,
one
that clearly runs counter to the interests of the German people.
#Japan
• We have not taken a single step toward worsening Russia-Japan relations. We treated them with great care.
Everything happening now in Russia-Japan relations
,
including their deterioration
,
is entirely of the Japanese government’s making
.

🇷🇺
🇰🇬
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin during the meeting with President of Kyrgyzstan Sadyr Japarov
(Bishkek, September 1, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
Russian-Kyrgyz relations of strategic partnership and alliance are developing successfully on the basis of
long-standing traditions of friendship, mutual respect and consideration for each other’s interests
.
You and I personally oversee the key issues of bilateral cooperation
. We will have another opportunity to meet later this year at
the Collective Security Treaty Organization Summit
and at
the traditional year-end meeting of CIS Leaders
– hopefully in St Petersburg, as has traditionally been the case, including
last year
.
📈
Russia is among the Republic’s leading trade partners
, accounting for
more than 26%
of its foreign trade. In 2025, bilateral trade
increased by 25.9%
and
grew by another 36%
in January-June 2026. This is a strong result.
Around 98%
of all payments are made in national currencies.
Accumulated Russian investment in Kyrgyzstan’s economy
has exceeded $1.2 billion
.
More than 2,000 companies with Russian capital operate in the country
. The Intergovernmental Commission is working effectively, and the 2022-2026 economic cooperation programme is being implemented.
In August, Issyk-Kul hosted
the Russian–Kyrgyz Interregional Conference
and
the Russian–Kyrgyz Economic Forum
.
More than 80 regions of Russia maintain ties with all seven regions of the Republic
.
🤝
We greatly appreciate your attention to supporting the Russian language
, which has official status in the Republic.
In 2023, you and I launched the construction of nine secondary schools in Kyrgyzstan
with Russian as the language of teaching. We expect the first three to open by September 1 of the next academic year, in 2027.
More than 10,000 Kyrgyz citizens
are studying in Russia, while
another 8,500 students
attend the Kyrgyz-Russian University in Bishkek.
We pay particular attention to security cooperation
. The Joint Russian Military Base stationed in the Republic is an important element in ensuring stability in the region.
We now have a good opportunity to discuss all these and other important issues.

🇷🇺
🇦🇲
Opening remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin during the meeting with Prime Minister of Armenia Nikol Pashinyan
(Bishkek, September 1, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
We have always supported and continue to support
the development of friendly and mutually beneficial relations with Armenia
, based on the principles of strategic partnership and alliance.
Russia is the Republic’s leading trade and economic partner
, accounting for
around 30% of its trade
, as well as a major investor in Armenia’s economy. In the first half of 2026, bilateral trade reached
$2.5 billion
.
Russian companies are among the largest taxpayers in Armenia
, creating jobs, transferring advanced technologies and strengthening the country’s energy security.
I would also note that you and I have discussed on a number of occasions
matters related to Armenia’s stated intention to join the EU
, both
by telephone
and
in person
.
☝️
You are well aware of Russia’s position:
Armenia’s aspiration to join the EU
is the natural and legitimate right of the country and its people
. Armenia is a sovereign state, and it is for the Armenian people to determine the path of their development.
At the same time, this undoubtedly creates difficulties for Armenia’s continued membership in
the Eurasian Economic Union
(
#EAEU
) and
risks nullifying the advantages
the Republic enjoys in the EAEU market and
disrupting established trade chains
.
📈
Meanwhile, over more than 10 years of participation in Eurasian integration processes,
Armenia’s GDP has nearly tripled: from $10.6 billion in 2015 to $29.2 billion in 2025
– at least according to our statistics. Exports to the EAEU countries
have increased tenfold
, and today the EAEU accounts for
around 36%
of Armenia’s foreign trade.
Therefore, of course,
the people of Armenia should clearly express their view
on the country’s future political and economic course
. At the same time, as we have discussed, any corresponding decisions should be approached strictly objectively and based on realities.
I remember that you publicly said you considered it necessary to hold a referendum on this issue
, and
I supported your position at the latest meeting of the Supreme Eurasian Economic Council
. I specifically mentioned that Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan had announced this publicly and urged our colleagues to support it as well.
👉
The sooner we determine the way forward, the better
, because we also need to understand how to develop our relations with Armenia, above all in the economic sphere.
Some regulatory matters
– agricultural products, various technical norms and standards, for example –
are fundamentally different in the EAEU and the EU
.
I hope that today, in a calm, friendly and businesslike atmosphere, we will discuss all these matters.
